messages:
Alex C: FYI AcmeGames reporting bursts of 429s every minute since ~03:20 UTC. Seems to line up with their keepalive/heartbeat job.
Jordan O: thanks — any quick logs or headers from their side?
Support Agent: pasted what we got from their proxy logs: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200/min`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 30` — they hit the limit exactly on minute boundaries.
Maria P: ok minute-boundary hits usually mean many small clients or a synchronized cron/heartbeat. Do we know if they use our SDK or direct HTTP?
Alex C: they use a homegrown client over HTTP/2 with persistent connections + periodic keepalives.
SRE-Bot: alert posted: "rate_limit_exceed: key=acct_acmegames, route=/v1/chat/stream, rpm=1240"
Priya L: can they be hitting a per-key aggregate? Our per-key RPM applies across regions/streams. If they multiplex streams, each stream still counts tokens/requests toward the same key.
Support Agent: I asked for a short repro script from them. They sent this snippet:```bash
for i in {1..65}; do curl -s -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate; done
```
Jordan O: that loop will blast the minute window. If their keepalive runs from many hosts at the same second, it stacks.
Alex C: asked them to run this lighter probe to confirm bucket smoothing:```bash
for i in {1..10}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme" -d '{"prompt":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate; sleep 2; done
```
Maria P: also requested they capture response headers on the 429s. Sometimes proxies swallow our X-RateLimit headers. If we don't see headers, harder to map to RPM vs burst cap.
Support Agent: they returned one 429 with headers:```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 13
Retry-After: 13
Content-Type: application/json
```
Priya L: good — this shows minute quota exhaustion (Reset in seconds). Repro steps seem consistent.
Jordan O: quick checklist for customers hitting minute windows: 1) verify single API key aggregation across all hosts, 2) avoid synchronized crons, 3) add random jitter/offset to keepalive, 4) use exponential backoff with full-jitter on 429, 5) reduce per-second concurrency or request folding.
Alex C: asked them to stagger their keepalive with jitter and reduce per-host rate by 30% for testing.
Support Agent: they tried stagger + jitter, immediate improvement — 429 count dropped ~90% in 10 minutes.
Maria P: recommend longer-term: 1) adopt client-side token bucket smoothing, 2) consider dedicated capacity if they need sustained high RPM, 3) we can do a temporary quota bump for a few hours while they re-architect.
Priya L: added note about HTTP/2: multiplexing doesn't circumvent per-key quotas. Too many concurrent streams can cause many requests to coincide when a heartbeat loops.
Jordan O: posted a small repro to run against staging to emulate their pattern (runs 60 parallel short requests at t=0 every minute). Sharing in case infra wants to run:```python
import requests, time, threading

def blast():
  r = requests.post("https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", headers={"Authorization":"Bearer sk-test"}, json={"prompt":"x"})
  print(r.status_code, r.headers.get('X-RateLimit-Remaining'))

while True:
  threads = [threading.Thread(target=blast) for _ in range(60)]
  for t in threads: t.start()
  for t in threads: t.join()
  time.sleep(60 - (time.time() % 60))
```
Alex C: ops ran that on a small canary and reproduced 429 spike. Confirmed behavior identical to customer.
Support Agent: Customer asked for immediate mitigation while they fix client: can we do a short soft-quota bump for their account?
Priya L: support policy: can offer a transient bump for 1-4 hours for production-impact cases; need billing ok. I can route to account manager.
Maria P: alternative quick fixes: route them to a higher-throughput model variant temporarily (compatibility check) or enable caching of repeated keepalive payloads on their side.
Jordan O: final note — updated the internal KB with this pattern: "synchronized heartbeats -> minute window 429s" and included recommended probes + repro script.
Alex C: closing loop with customer: they accepted jitter + temp bump while rolling out smoothing. Marking thread resolved but keeping logs for 24h. :white_check_mark:
